# ALLOCATIONS: what one parse allocates, per target (auto-generated)

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by `node test/alloc-work.ts --write`. Do not edit by hand. -->

The gate `alloc-work` (test/alloc-work.ts) regenerates this file and fails when it differs: an allocation
more or an allocation fewer than recorded both fail, so every change shows in this diff. The counts are exact:
TS target and emitted JS parser by instrumentation of the emitted module (test/alloc-instrument.ts), Go by
`runtime.MemStats` with the collector off. Bytes: Go exact (`TotalAlloc`); TS / JS modeled from V8's layout
(pointer compression; the model is in test/alloc-instrument.ts; the gate prints a measured `heapUsed` delta
beside it). One warm parse runs before the measured one; what a module builds once is not counted.

Go rows measured with go1.27.4. Which function an allocation is attributed to depends on the toolchain (one
commit: a 16 B slice growth in `(*engine).matchLit` under go1.27.4, in `(*engine).finish` under go1.26.11), so the
rows hold for this toolchain only. CI installs it (`actions/setup-go`, .github/workflows/ci.yml); with another one
the Go rows are NOT RUN.

Inputs (locked npm packages): `acorn@8.16.0` `dist/acorn.js`, `typescript@5.9.3` `lib/lib.es5.d.ts` and `lib/_tsserver.js` (also repeated 4×: per-token counts must not grow with size).

Modes. TS target: `parse(src)` (the CST built directly) and `parseWith(src, cstBuilder)` (through builder frames).
JS target: `fresh` = a new `createParser()` per parse, `reuse` = one parser, its document reused. Go: `fresh` = a new
`CstBuilder` per `ParseWith`, `reuse` = one kept. RESULT = what the returned tree holds (TS: objects reachable from
it; Go fresh: the final capacity of `Nodes` / `Kids` / `Toks`); OVERHEAD = everything else, garbage once the parse
returns. Tokens: each target's own `tokenize` count. Nodes: rule nodes of the result (JS, Go: the arena's node count).
